qa.name: Abductor Digiti Minimi
qa.origin: Pisiform and tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris
qa.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the little finger
qa.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Abduction of the little finger at the metacarpophalangeal joint
qa.clinical_note: Most medial hypothenar muscle — hypothenar wasting indicates ulnar nerve injury; the ulnar nerve and artery enter the hand through Guyon canal just lateral to the pisiform

qa.name: Flexor Digiti Minimi Brevis
qa.origin: Hook of the hamate and flexor retinaculum
qa.insertion: Medial side of the base of the proximal phalanx of the little finger
qa.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joint of the little finger
qa.clinical_note: Originates from the hook of the hamate — a fractured hook of hamate can compress the deep branch of the ulnar nerve causing hypothenar and intrinsic muscle weakness

qa.name: Opponens Digiti Minimi
qa.origin: Hook of the hamate and flexor retinaculum
qa.insertion: Medial border of the fifth metacarpal along its entire length
qa.innervation: Deep branch of the ulnar nerve
qa.function: Opposition of the little finger — draws the fifth metacarpal anteriorly and rotates it to face the thumb
qa.clinical_note: Deepest hypothenar muscle — mirrors opponens pollicis in structure and function; together they allow the palm to cup for gripping
